cards.explanation: The answer is Mockers, friends. The psalm says the blessed man does not "…sit in the seat of mockers." (Psalm 1:1) Walking, setting foot, sitting: that's three steps, and he skips all of them. I think that's a man who knows exactly where he's headed.

The answer is the Law of the LORD, friends. "…his delight is in the Law of the LORD…" (Psalm 1:2) Delight is a big word, and the psalm puts it right there. The verse goes on to say that "…on His law he meditates day and night." I think that's a man who really loves what the LORD has said.

The answer is by streams of water, friends. The tree is "…planted by streams of water…" (Psalm 1:3) The psalm puts it right there by the streams. I think that tree never has to wonder where its next drink is coming from.
The answer is False, friends. Psalm 1:3 says this tree's "…leaf does not wither…" The psalm says it plainly, so a withering leaf isn't in this verse. And I think that's one happy tree.

The answer is prospers, friends! The psalm says he "…prospers in all he does." (Psalm 1:3) That's a tree planted by water and a man who's planted in the LORD's law, both doing well. Fruit, leaves and all.

The answer is chaff driven off by the wind, friends! Psalm 1:4 says, "Not so the wicked! For they are like chaff driven off by the wind." Chaff is the light, dry husk, so there's nothing in it to hold it down. The tree stays put by the water, and the chaff goes wherever the wind says. I think those two pictures couldn't be more different.

The answer is False, friends. The psalm says "…the wicked will not stand in the judgment…" (Psalm 1:5) It follows right after the picture of chaff in the wind. They're not going to stand, just like chaff doesn't.

The answer is True, friends! Psalm 1:6 says "…the LORD guards the path of the righteous…" Think about that for a second. The LORD is the one doing the guarding. That's good news for anybody on that road.

The answer is that it will perish, friends. Psalm 1:6 says "…but the way of the wicked will perish." The psalm starts with a man who is blessed, and it ends with the way of the wicked perishing. The LORD guards one path, and the other path perishes.
